headline.text: The Spanish label says carbamazepine may reduce amitriptyline-class drug concentrations and antidepressant response.

reported.text: The label describes reduced tricyclic antidepressant concentrations and response with carbamazepine.

mechanism.text: The label attributes the reduction to increased tricyclic antidepressant metabolism.

claims.text: The Spanish amitriptyline label says carbamazepine may increase tricyclic antidepressant metabolism, reducing plasma concentrations and antidepressant response.
claims.quote: la carbamazepina y la hierba de San Juan (Hypericum perforatum) pueden aumentar el metabolismo de los antidepresivos tricíclicos, con la consiguiente reducción de sus concentraciones plasmáticas y de la respuesta antidepresiva.
claims.quoteEnglish: Carbamazepine and St John's wort (Hypericum perforatum) may increase the metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants, consequently reducing their plasma concentrations and antidepressant response.
claims.judgeRationale: The amitriptyline SmPC lists carbamazepine among inducers that may increase TCA metabolism, reducing plasma concentrations and antidepressant response; the rendering is faithful.

pharmacistQuestions.text: The label describes this interaction, but there seem to be no human studies of it. How is it usually handled for someone like me?
Do any of my other medicines contain Amitriptyline or Carbamazepine, or work the same way?
Does my dose, or the time between taking Amitriptyline and Carbamazepine, change how much this matters?

gaps.text: The packet contains no controlled human study isolating the amitriptyline–carbamazepine interaction.
